title: Final Parking Space: 1986 Chrysler Laser XT Turbo

body_markdown:
If you want to buy a new 2027 Chrysler, there is but one choice:[the Pacifica minivan](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-chrysler-pacifica-gets-a-fancy-blue-interior-to-go-with-its-new-face/) . Time-travel back 40 years, though, and you’d find that American Chrysler dealers[offered](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Chrysler_and_Imperial/1986-Chrysler/index.html) sedans with both front- and rear-wheel-drive, coupes, convertibles, wagons,[a limousine](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Chrysler_and_Imperial/1984_Chrysler/1984-Chrysler-Executive-Cars-Brochure/index.html) , and even an evil-looking turbocharged sports car. I’ve found one of the last machines, an absolutely *loaded*[Laser XT](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Chrysler_and_Imperial/1986-Chrysler/1986%20Chrysler%20Laser/index.html) at[a car graveyard just south of Denver](https://coloradoautoandparts.com/#navigation) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The Chrysler Laser was at heart a luxed-up[Dodge Daytona](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/this-11000-dodge-daytona-shelby-z-is-a-foil-for-montereys-big-money/) , and thus a member of the extended[K-Car](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/how-the-k-car-saved-chrysler/) family.


Chrysler Corporation


It was sold for the 1984 through 1986 model years, after which it was replaced by the restyled[LeBaron Coupe](https://www.autoblog.com/news/junkyard-gem-1987-chrysler-lebaron-coupe/) . Chrysler marketed it as “the first sports car to bear the Chrysler name.”


Chrysler hired[the voice of Darth Vader](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c903841w145o) to narrate Laser commercials. “Beats Mustang GT, Mazda RX-7, and Trans-Am in the slalom!”


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


For 1986, the Laser XT listed at $11,854, or about $36,320. That was more than the cost of a[Mustang GT](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/fox-body-buyers-guide/) ($10,691) and just a bit less than the price tag on the[Camaro Z28](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/third-gen-camaro-1982-92-the-one-thats-misunderstood/) ($11,902). Both of those cars had V-8s with more power than the Laser XT’s turbocharged four-cylinder, driving the rear wheels, but they also weighed quite a bit more.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This car has some extras that would have pushed its final price much higher. In addition to the[Mark Cross Corinthian Leather](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Chrysler_and_Imperial/1986-Chrysler/1986%20Chrysler%20Laser/slides/1986%20Chrysler%20Laser%20Brochure%2008-09.html) interior with “enthusiast” driver’s seat ($567), there’s the “T-Bar” roof.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Chrysler charged $332 for the factory removable glass T-tops, but this car received the aftermarket treatment from Cars & Concepts.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This[AM/FM/cassette radio](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ) with joystick balance/fader control cost $244, while the air conditioning was a cool $757. Just these few items would have resulted in a price well over 40 grand in today’s money.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The engine is a 2.2-liter turbocharged SOHC four-cylinder rated at 146 horsepower and 170 pound-feet of torque. With a curb weight of just 2695 pounds, this was a quick car in its day.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The hood vent is functional, sending outside air into the cleaner intake.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The base transmission was a five-speed manual, with a three-speed Torqueflite automatic available as a $504 option.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


It was built at[St. Louis Assembly](https://www.allpar.com/threads/chrysler%E2%80%99s-st-louis-plants-fenton-missouri.229412/) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


It was sold new at Jess Hull Chrysler-Plymouth in Englewood, Colorado, now the site of a Sprouts Farmers Market. As the junkyard crow flies, this car’s Final Parking Space is less than a mile away from where it was purchased.


Chrysler Corporation


Chrysler Corporation revived the Laser name for the 1990 model year, on the Plymouth-badged sibling to the Mitsubishi Eclipse and Eagle Talon. Ford[used the Laser name](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PWS1K5u4P6A) on cars from the early 1980s through the mid-2000s, but never in North America.


James Earl Jones: “Because the competition is hot, we had to be hotter.” Did this ad come out before or after[the amazing “Cocaine Factory” commercial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tSbDa9REOjM) for the 1985 Plymouth Turismo Duster?
